You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task-8513899a — observed pattern

Solved test confirmed correct with zero wrong attempts, after 4 demo requests.

## Reliable rule for the solved test
The grid has background color 4 and patterned/stripe color 5. In rows that begin with a run/pattern of 5s and then end in a suffix of 4s, recolor that trailing 4 suffix to 1. Preserve the preceding 5 cells and all other rows/cells. Fully uniform 4 rows and the fully uniform 5 row remain unchanged.

Test rows (0-based):
- Row 0: cols 0–6 are 5, cols 7–14 were 4; output changes cols 7–14 to 1.
- Row 6: same as row 0; changes cols 7–14 to 1.
- Row 9: cols 0–12 are 5, cols 13–14 were 4; changes cols 13–14 to 1.
All other rows remain as input. This exact output was accepted.

## Demonstration evidence / cautious generalization
Across demos, color 1 marks trailing/incomplete portions of repeated patterned bands, while the base patterned cells and complete rows stay unchanged. Demo 4 had repeated 3×12 patterned blocks with 9-pattern cells and a contrasting suffix; suffixes in the top and bottom copies were changed to 1, while the complete middle block was untouched. Other demos show the same general idea with different layouts and colors, so the broader rule may be to mark the incomplete/remainder portions of a repeating pattern with 1. However, exact cross-layout mechanism isn't fully established; use the test's simple row-wise suffix case directly when it appears.

Avoid relying on the prior version of this note: it described an unrelated test and had incorrect dimensions/colors. For future similar instances, identify the dominant background and stripe pattern, inspect repeated rows for a trailing background-color suffix, and recolor only those suffix cells to 1. Preserve grid dimensions and everything else.
